decision: Which lifecycle email sequences are we missing, in what order should we build them, and are new users getting too many emails?
limitations: Send load uses default email counts and day windows per sequence unless you pass --emails, and assumes every sequence reaches every new user. It counts no transactional or product email, so the real inbox load is higher.
Breakeven uses one build cost for every sequence and is judged against monthly signups. Win-back and sunset run on lapsed users, a smaller base, so judge those against that base.
It does not estimate lift. It gives the extra conversions a month a sequence needs to pay back; whether that is plausible for your audience is your call.

Input it doesn't recognise (JSON, or a misspelled flag) is ignored without an error and the audit runs on defaults (500 signups, $400 a conversion, nothing built). Check the result reflects your numbers.
review: The lifecycle or CRM owner lists every email that already fires, transactional included, with the real email count per sequence, before trusting the send-load verdict. They confirm the value per conversion before the breakeven decides what gets built.
